sections.html:
Albany is the seat of Albany County, with Colonie to the north, Guilderland to the west and Bethlehem to the south. Renters outnumber owners here. Owners live in just 38.2% of homes, and a typical owned home is worth $234,700. The city had an estimated 101,698 residents in mid-2025, spread over 44,357 households of about two people each.

Buyers shop by neighborhood first: Arbor Hill, Center Square, Pine Hills and the South End are among the best known. Name the neighborhood in any listing or offer conversation. If your building has tenants, expect questions about leases and inspection certificates early on.

sections.h2: Registries that can hold up a closing
sections.html:
The city's Buildings and Regulatory Compliance department keeps several registries. When a registration expires, a hold goes on the property record and no permits issue until the lapse is fixed.

Albany registry costs for a one to three unit house
RegistryWhat it costsHow often
Vacant building$250 first year, $500 second, $750 third, then $1,000Renew yearly
Rental unit certificate$50 a unitInspection every 24 months
Waste collection fee$180 a unit, on the tax billYearly, new in 2026

The vacant building rule dates to July 1, 2000. Register as soon as a building empties, or when you buy an empty one. Not registering risks a penalty of up to $1,000 a day. An unpaid waste fee moves to the next bill with late charges.

Red placards on some empty buildings tell firefighters about structural hazards. If one of those is yours, ask the department where the registration stands before you take an offer.

The city requires the vacant building registration to stay current, but it does not require repairs before a sale. A buyer who takes the house as is inherits the registration duty, so confirm the annual fee is paid before closing.

Larger and non-residential buildings pay more under the city's schedule. If the house has been empty for a while, call the department, ask for the current registration status in writing and bring that paper to the title company.

sections.h2: How to challenge your Albany assessment
sections.html:
Complaints can be filed from May 1 until the fourth Tuesday in May. The next window opens May 1, 2027, and the form is RP-524. There is no filing charge, and the Assessor's Office at City Hall has forms starting May 1.

New construction, fires, demolitions and periodic citywide updates are what move an assessment. If your records show a change like that, tell the assessor, because buyers see the same number you do.

Exemption applications, Basic STAR included, are accepted January 1 through March 1, and all owners sign. A buyer who wants a STAR or senior exemption applies on their own after the deed, so mention the March 1 date if your sale lands in winter.

A city bill can be split. Half is due January 31 (February 6 for eligible seniors) and the rest is billed in July. Split payments are limited to check or cash, and online payment covers only full amounts. Mailed payments count on the postmark, so skip bill-pay services that do not use one.

Before you close, have the title company check the city bill, the waste collection fee and the school tax line by line. Each can carry a different balance, and a payoff that covers only one of them leaves the others to surface later.

sections.h2: What does an Albany sale cost in state tax?
sections.html:
The state transfer tax is $2 per $500 of the sale price and is usually the seller's cost. The Albany County Clerk receives the TP-584 return and payment within 15 days of the deed. A 1% mansion tax applies to residences of $1 million or more and is paid by the buyer.

Going through an agent means preparing the house, hosting showings and waiting on a buyer's lender. A cash purchase skips that and closes when you pick, which fits an empty house, a lapsed rental certificate or an estate.

sections.h2: Documents to gather before you sell
sections.html:
Either way, pull together the same paperwork:

  • The deed and your lender's payoff letter
  • The most recent city and school tax bills
  • Proof that registry certificates are current, including any rental registration or certificate of occupancy paperwork
  • Leases and the latest rental dwelling certificate, if tenants live there, so a buyer can see the inspection status at a glance

Having these in one folder shortens the title search. It also speeds a cash offer, because the buyer can price the house without waiting on records from three different offices.

faqs.q: Can I sell a vacant house in Albany without fixing it first?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires the vacant building registration to stay current, but it does not require repairs before a sale. A buyer who takes the house as is inherits the registration duty, so confirm the annual fee is paid before closing.
The fourth Tuesday in May, with the window opening May 1. The next one opens May 1, 2027. Forms are available from the Assessor's Office at City Hall beginning May 1.

faqs.q: How much is the vacant building fee in Albany?
faqs.a: For a one to three unit residential building it is $250 in the first year, $500 in the second, $750 in the third and $1,000 for each later year. Larger and non-residential buildings pay more under the city's schedule.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay New York's transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller pays the base state transfer tax of $2 per $500, unless the contract says otherwise. The 1% mansion tax applies to residences of $1 million or more and is paid by the buyer.

faqs.q: What documents should an Albany seller have ready?
faqs.a: Bring the deed, the most recent city and school tax bills, proof that registry certificates are current, any rental registration or certificate of occupancy paperwork, and a mortgage payoff statement. If tenants live there, add leases and the rental dwelling certificate.
